es: Resolver una ronda de preguntas sorpresa con respuestas estructuradas, una reparación y una reformulación.

teaching.explanationEs: Con presión, sigue el orden que ya conoces.

teaching.explanationEs: Instead of + -ing: reformular mantiene la conversación viva.

feedback.es: Cada fórmula tiene su función: tricky one gana tiempo, I meant repara, rephrase reformula e in short cierra.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué corrige el hablante.

choices.text: He changes his stance on cars.
He corrects the month of his example.
He corrects the name of a place.

feedback.es: Tras «Sorry, I meant June, not May» cambia el mes del ejemplo, no su postura.

origin.audio: Should cities ban cars? Hmm, that's a tricky one. My stance is yes. The main reason is air quality. For example, my city closed its old town to cars in May, and the air improved. Sorry, I meant June, not May. In short, fewer cars mean cleaner air.

prompt.es: Completa: «quería decir el viernes» y «déjame reformular».

feedback.es: I meant rectifica un dato y let me rephrase introduce otra versión.

sentences: Let me ___ that in one sentence.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase cierra con una síntesis tras la respuesta?

choices.text: By the way, I also like pasta.
Anyway, I forgot what I wanted to say.
To recap, cooking saves money and builds a good habit.

feedback.es: To recap resume la idea en una frase; las otras abren un desvío o muestran desorden.

prompt.es: Responde a tres preguntas sorpresa: estructura, una reparación y una reformulación.

answer.text: Thanks, that's a tricky first question, so let me think. My stance is that everyone should learn to cook. The main reason is that it saves money. For example, I cook on Sundays, sorry, I meant Saturdays, and I spend half as much on food. In short, cooking is a useful habit. Second question. Hang on, let me gather my thoughts. I would say that a library is better than home for studying, because nobody interrupts you. For example, last month I finished my project in two afternoons there. Let me rephrase that: a quiet place helps you focus, and the library gives you one. Third question, what would I change in my city? Off the top of my head, I would build more bike lanes. The reason is that they make streets safer. For example, accidents fell in my neighbourhood after the new lane opened. To recap, cooking saves money, libraries help you focus and bike lanes make cities safer. My point is that small habits and small changes matter.
accepted: Thanks, that's a tricky first question, so let me think. My stance is that everyone should learn to cook. The main reason is that it saves money. For example, I cook on Sundays, sorry, I meant Saturdays, and I spend half as much on food. In short, cooking is a useful habit. Second question. Hang on, let me gather my thoughts. I would say that a library is better than home for studying, because nobody interrupts you. For example, last month I finished my project in two afternoons there. Let me rephrase that: a quiet place helps you focus, and the library gives you one. Third question, what would I change in my city? Off the top of my head, I would build more bike lanes. The reason is that they make streets safer. For example, accidents fell in my neighbourhood after the new lane opened. To recap, cooking saves money, libraries help you focus and bike lanes make cities safer. My point is that small habits and small changes matter.

Let me think for a second. My view is that everybody should learn to cook. The first reason is that it is healthier, because you choose what goes into your food. For example, my brother started cooking at home last year, and he has felt better since then. Sorry, I meant two years ago. So, in conclusion, cooking is good for your health. For the second question, I believe a library is better for studying. Because it is quiet, you can focus for longer. Let me put that another way: a library removes distractions. For the third question, I would change the bus system in my city. The main reason is that buses are often late. For instance, last week my bus arrived twenty minutes late. To sum up, good food, a quiet place to study and better buses would make daily life easier.

feedback.es: Una buena ronda responde con estructura, repara un error, reformula una idea y termina recapitulando.

origin.text: Preguntas: 1) ¿Debería todo el mundo aprender a cocinar? 2) ¿Es mejor estudiar en casa o en una biblioteca? 3) ¿Qué cambiarías de tu ciudad? Escribe unas 130–300 palabras: responde a las tres con postura, razón y ejemplo, incluye una reparación (Sorry, I meant…) y una reformulación (Let me rephrase that) y cierra recapitulando.
